column1: # product    Essenthos/sources/door43-projects.tsv
# producer   by hand
# The translationCore projects on git.door43.org in which people aligned a book of a text word by word on their own, outside
#   the release the text's interlinear comes from (the Ohienko's is uk_ts/uk_ubio): the same base text, the same USFM 3
#   alignment, a different person and often different terms (TSK-1905, Resources/Door43/LICENCE.md). Nobody checked them, so
#   a project is read only after its links were read by hand. One row per project, pinned to a commit and each file to the
#   SHA-256 it had then; scripts/fetch-door43-ohienko-books.ps1 fetches every row into Door43/uk_ubio_books, and stated-pairs
#   reads the rows with read t (Door43AlignmentSource). Edit a row, fetch, and run forge build.
# Columns: text (whose words it ties); file (under Door43/uk_ubio_books: the Paratext number and code of the book); book (its
#   English name, as its links' source says it); repository (owner/name; the owner is the person who aligned it); commit;
#   licence (as the project's LICENSE.md and manifest state it: CC0 1.0 or CC BY-SA 4.0, each credited by a dataset); read
#   (t: its links are read); book_sha256, licence_sha256, manifest_sha256 (the aligned book translationCore exported, the
#   project's LICENSE.md and manifest.json at the commit); milestones (the alignment milestones the book holds); reason.
